GROUP_PINNING.TITLE: Group Pinning
GROUP_PINNING.SUBTITLE: Lock a model to specific provider groups and their rates instead of automatic cheapest routing.
GROUP_PINNING.P_OVERVIEW_1: Every model is served by one or more provider groups, each with its own price. By default a key uses auto: every request routes to the cheapest group that is currently live.
GROUP_PINNING.P_OVERVIEW_2: Pinning overrides this per model: you pick exactly which groups it may use, and billing is locked to their rates. Useful when you need a specific provider's quality or region, or a rate that must not drift.
GROUP_PINNING.P_PRICES_1: Each model's detail page lists every group with its input and output price under Group Pricing; the discount badge in the model list always reflects the cheapest group.
GROUP_PINNING.ALT_GROUP_PRICES: Group pricing table on a model detail page
GROUP_PINNING.P_PINNING_1: Open API Keys, create or edit a key, and open the group selector. Search for a model, click it, and tick one or more provider groups, sorted cheapest first with their rate multiplier. Models you leave alone stay on auto.
GROUP_PINNING.ALT_MAPPING: Per-model provider group picker in the key editor
GROUP_PINNING.P_PINNING_2: Pinned models float to the top with a badge showing how many groups they are locked to, and Clear all resets the key to full auto. The key list shows pinned keys as auto +N.
GROUP_PINNING.P_ROUTING_1: A pinned model routes only within its pinned groups: the cheapest is tried first with automatic failover to the next on errors or downtime. Whatever group actually serves the request is the rate that gets billed.
GROUP_PINNING.P_ROUTING_2: An explicit X-Group header on a request still wins over the pin, and unpinned models keep cheapest-available routing.
GROUP_PINNING.P_ERRORS_1: If every pinned group for a model is down while other providers still serve it, requests fail with a targeted error instead of a generic busy message:
GROUP_PINNING.P_ERRORS_2: Widen or remove the pin on the key, or retry later. The model itself is still up.

ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.TITLE: Errors & Rate Limits
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.SUBTITLE: What each status code means and what to do about it.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_ENVELOPE_1: Errors come back as JSON in the OpenAI error format. The message states what happened, code is a stable machine-readable identifier, and a request id is appended to every message:
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_ENVELOPE_2: Always include the request id when you contact support or open a Discord ticket. It lets us find your exact request in the logs.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_STATUS_CODES_1: The status codes you will actually encounter:
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_400_MEANING: Invalid request: bad parameter values (for example max_tokens below the model minimum) or a prompt blocked by content moderation.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_400_ACTION: Fix the request. Retrying unchanged will fail again.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_401_MEANING: Key problem: missing, invalid, expired or disabled API key.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_401_ACTION: Check the Authorization header and your key on the Tokens page.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_402_MEANING: This key's own spending limit is exhausted.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_402_ACTION: Raise the key's limit or create a new key.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_403_MEANING: Access denied: account balance empty, model not allowed for this key, or your IP is not on the key's allowlist.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_403_ACTION: Top up, or check the key's model and IP restrictions.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_413_MEANING: Request too large for this model's free trial cap.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_413_ACTION: Shorten the prompt or switch to the paid model.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_429_MEANING: A rate limit fired (see the kinds below).
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_429_ACTION: Wait for Retry-After seconds, then retry or switch models.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_500_MEANING: Something failed on our side or at the upstream provider.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_500_ACTION: Retry after a short wait; persistent 500s are worth a report.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_503_MEANING: All providers for the model are busy, or the model name does not exist.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.R_503_ACTION: Read the message: busy resolves in minutes, a typo does not.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_BUSY_VS_UNKNOWN_1: Two very different situations share status 503. The first is temporary congestion:
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_BUSY_VS_UNKNOWN_2: The code get_channel_failed (all providers busy) means every free provider for that model is momentarily rate limited. This auto-recovers within minutes: retry or switch models. The code model_not_found (not offered here) means the model name itself does not resolve, and retrying will never help. Check for typos or look up the current name in the catalog.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_BUSY_VS_UNKNOWN_3: Treat 503 with get_channel_failed as retry/fallback and 503 with model_not_found as a hard error in your client.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_RATE_LIMITS_1: A 429 can come from several layers:
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.L_RATE_LIMITS_OURS: Our free-model cap: 1 request per minute per free model per user. A fairness cap so shared pools survive peak hours.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.L_RATE_LIMITS_UPSTREAM: Upstream provider limits: the provider behind a free model hit its own cap ("temporarily rate-limited upstream").
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.L_RATE_LIMITS_DAILY: Daily token budgets on some free pools; these reset at midnight UTC.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.L_RATE_LIMITS_TPM: Tokens-per-minute caps that trigger on very large prompts.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.L_RATE_LIMITS_CONCURRENCY: A per-user concurrency limit when too many requests run in parallel.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_RATE_LIMITS_2: Paid models have no {appName}-imposed rate limits.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_FREE_MODEL_LIMIT_1: When our 1-per-minute cap fires you get standard rate-limit headers, so clients can back off precisely:
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_FREE_MODEL_LIMIT_2: Retry-After is dynamic: the actual seconds left in your window, not a flat 60. The error message also names the paid twin of the model, which has no limit.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_TRIAL_CAPS_1: Some normally-paid models are offered free with a request size cap. Oversized prompts get 413 with a message like: Request body too large for gpt-4.1 model. Max size: 8000 tokens.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_TRIAL_CAPS_2: The cap applies to the free trial route only; the paid model takes full-length prompts.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_RETRIES_1: Honor Retry-After on 429. Retry 503 get_channel_failed after a short wait, or fall back to another model. Do not retry 400-class errors, they are deterministic.
ERRORS_AND_RATE_LIMITS.P_RETRIES_2: Failed and refused requests are not billed: any pre-hold on your balance is refunded when the request errors.

DISCORD_REWARDS.P_OVERVIEW_2: Every successful payout is sent to you as a DM and announced in the public grants log, so payments are always visible. Amounts are server-configured and can change; the values below are the current ones.
DISCORD_REWARDS.P_LINK_1: No reward can reach your balance until your Discord account is linked to your {appName} account in the settings. After linking, claim the one-time connect bonus on the verify panel in the server.
DISCORD_REWARDS.P_LINK_2: A reward earned before linking is not lost: link your account, then press the Redeem reward button on the reward message and it pays out.

DISCORD_REWARDS.P_NOTIF_2: Recurring reward DMs (vote, invite, level and boost) can be muted per event type with the bot command:
